consensus_summary: Fig leaves symbolize inadequate human efforts to cover sin and shame, commonly expressed as self-righteousness; leaves without fruit can also symbolize outward religious show without genuine substance.
book_summary: Fig leaves signify self-made righteousness: a self-fashioned covering that has outward appearance but no genuine spiritual substance.
consensus_core_identification: Inadequate self-made righteousness or human self-covering.
book_core_identification: Self-made righteousness as an insubstantial covering.
boundary_disagreement: No material boundary disagreement. The book combines the Genesis self-covering motif with the Gospel motif of leaves without fruit, both already recognized in the consensus.
material_contradiction: None. The book’s identification directly matches the consensus primary meaning and incorporates a common listed alternative.
rationale: Reduced to their minimum cores, both identify fig leaves with self-made, inadequate righteousness or covering. The book’s phrase “all show and no substance” draws on the fruitless fig tree, but the consensus explicitly recognizes outward religious appearance without fruit and notes that this motif is often blended with the Genesis interpretation. This is elaboration rather than a changed identification or extension.
strongest_objection: Genesis 3:7 describes improvised covering but does not explicitly identify it as righteousness or declare it inadequate, while Matthew 21:19 concerns a fruitless fig tree rather than Adam and Eve’s covering. The citations support the component images, but the unified doctrine of self-made righteousness is interpretive.
